content.text: Setting up a [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/sovereign-commerce-infrastructure-digital-creators-honest-side-side|COREMERCH guide to sovereign]] digital store is a four-step sequence that most creators overcomplicate by starting in the wrong order. Step one is the backend: Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script handles [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-what-actually-how-5|USDT Payment]]-gateways-cameroon-digital-products-what-nobody-tells|payment]] verification, order logging, and product delivery. Step two is the payment layer: NOWPayments connects your wallet addresses to the checkout flow — no KYC required from you or your buyer. Step three is the storefront: Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages serves your store for free with no server management. Step four is testing: complete a real mainnet transaction, confirm the webhook fires, the order logs, and the delivery email arrives with a working download link. Only after step four passes cleanly should you promote the store. COREMERCH deploys the complete Edge Stack — Cloudflare Pages plus Workers plus Supabase plus NOWPayments — in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

When platforms like Stripe reject digital creators due to country or platform restrictions, it's time to build a sovereign digital store that puts you in control. The key to this infrastructure is the combination of GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and Supabase for the order database. This setup allows you to deploy your store in 4-6 hours with Stack 01, or in 48 hours with Stack 02, without relying on a centralized platform like Stripe. By leveraging the power of GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, you can host your digital store for free, and with NOWPayments, you can accept crypto payments without any transaction fees. The Supabase order database ensures that all your orders are securely stored and easily accessible, giving you complete control over your digital store.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your sovereign digital store, you'll need to set up a GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages account, depending on the hosting platform you choose. You'll also need to install the NOWPayments plugin on your store, which allows you to accept crypto payments. Additionally, you'll need to configure Supabase for your order database, which involves setting up a new project, creating a table for orders, and configuring the API keys. Lastly, you'll need to deploy your Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script backend logic, which will handle tasks such as order processing and payment verification.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to configure NOWPayments to work with your Supabase order database. This involves setting up a webhook to automatically send payment confirmations to your Supabase project, and configuring your Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script backend logic to process payments and deliver your digital products. You'll also need to configure your Supabase project to store orders securely, which involves setting up a new table for orders and configuring the API keys. By following these steps, you'll have a seamless payment and delivery pipeline that works independently of Stripe or any other centralized platform.
By building a sovereign digital store with Supabase, you can accept crypto payments without relying on a centralized platform like Stripe.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, it's time to go live with your digital store. To do this, you'll need to deploy your Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script backend logic, which will handle tasks such as order processing and payment verification. You'll also need to configure your NOWPayments plugin to accept crypto payments, and set up a new project in Supabase to store your orders. By following these steps, you'll be able to process your first transaction and start selling your digital products to customers around the world.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your infrastructure is running, you can start scaling your digital store to meet the demands of your growing customer base. To do this, you'll need to upgrade your hosting plan with GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, and configure your Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script backend logic to handle increased traffic. You'll also need to add more products to your store, and configure your Supabase project to store more orders securely. By following these steps, you'll be able to scale your digital store and meet the demands of your growing customer base.
